answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small bond locked on a shared bridge contract before it can trade. Reputation then accrues per vertex of proven work, not per account: a fresh vertex with no history earns nothing until peers attest its output. Honest agents build a terrace of attestations over time, while an attacker splitting into many cheap identities must fund every bond and still earns no attestation without real work, so faking scale costs more than it returns.
